newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 12.2 percent.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday program trading averaged 12.2 percent of its average daily volume of 455.8 million, or 55.7 million shares a day, during the week of December 9-13.
Buy programs accounted for a daily average of 24.7 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average of 31.0 million shares.
In all markets, program trading during the week of December 9-13 averaged 92.4 million shares a day.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Goldman Sachs, Interactive Brokers and Susquehanna Brokerage Services executed all of most of their program activity for customers. Morgan Stanley split its program activity between its own account and those of customers.
During that week, 23.6 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage and another 1.4 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses portfolio trading strategies involving the purchase or sale of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a total value of $1 million or more.
